scope: Adaptive forecast validation and mixture infrastructure for Simfolio; no numerical-source or production changes.

snapshot.forecast_unit: joint asset portfolio path with within-path accounting
snapshot.inner_mixture_objective: endpoint CRPS represented by w^T A - 0.5 w^T B w
snapshot.external_decision_score: Unchanged canonical lead-weighted marginal CRPS over cumulative portfolio-return distributions: training-SD times square-root-lead normalization and normalized log-calendar lead weights; the marginals are generated from coherent joint asset paths and within-path accounting, but the score does not directly assess cross-horizon or cross-asset dependence.
snapshot.reported_development: 14.61% better on 355 reused development requests; exploratory, not broad or full-panel proof

historical_scope_note: Local selector receipts describe a prior capped-origin prototype and diagnostic-only full-history selector. Keep those separate from the current user-supplied 355-request result.

experiments.contrast: Current horizon-shortening/non-overlap scheme versus rolling-origin training on all available origins at the actual requested horizon, with time-block/HAC uncertainty for overlap.
experiments.hypothesis: More observations at the actual target horizon can reduce weight-estimation variance without changing the forecasting task; shorter-H validation may choose weights that do not transfer to requested H.
experiments.training_protocol: At every historical forecast origin, use only the then-available fit history and candidate predictions for the exact requested H. Maintain overlapping and non-overlapping score summaries separately.
experiments.outer_gate: Matched requested-H requests scored by the unchanged canonical lead-weighted marginal CRPS over cumulative portfolio-return distributions, generated from coherent joint asset paths and within-path accounting, at the final path count.
experiments.cost: Forecast generation scales with added origin coverage when forecasts are absent; cached predictions make weight fitting and re-indexing cheap.
risks: Two non-overlapping folds give weak uncertainty information
Do not count assets as independent observations

experiments.contrast: Current per-request simplex weights versus training-estimated, partially pooled family masses and within-family weights over the frozen menu.
experiments.hypothesis: A hierarchical penalty can stabilize request-specific mixtures and avoid menu-multiplicity bias when similar recipes/families are correlated.
experiments.training_protocol: Use the existing recipe-family map; estimate a pooled center only from training origins; fit pooling strength with chronological inner folds; do not use last-winner fallback.
experiments.outer_gate: One locked mixture scored at the same matched requests and exact horizons with the unchanged canonical external marginal score.
experiments.cost: Low if paths are cached; solve a grouped convex optimization and record weight dispersion/effective recipe count.
risks: Excess pooling biases away from genuinely request-specific winners
Equal-weight point forecast evidence does not prove CRPS gains

experiments.contrast: Shared mixture vector versus a low-dimensional, partially pooled weight function of requested horizon, starting with log(H) and a small spline/random effect.
experiments.hypothesis: A smooth horizon gate may borrow evidence across sparse horizons while allowing stable changes in model performance.
experiments.training_protocol: One as-of-origin feature at a time; optionally add trailing volatility only after loss-difference diagnostics show repeatable heterogeneity. Use one gate per request and one expert selection for each complete joint portfolio path.
experiments.outer_gate: Same-horizon outer requests; unchanged canonical marginal score and coherent path/accounting contract.
experiments.cost: Small fit overhead on cached path forecasts; new forecasts needed only for absent horizon/origin cells.
risks: Per-asset or per-day weighting may invalidate joint paths
The canonical marginal CRPS does not assess cross-horizon or cross-asset dependence
sources: Berrisch and Ziel 2024 multivariate CRPS learning

experiments.contrast: Existing batch learner versus in-progress BOA using identical candidate paths and score definitions, with outcomes applied only when full-H labels mature.
experiments.hypothesis: A sequential learner may adapt more quickly to changing relative model skill than a batch fit over the full training history.
experiments.training_protocol: Replay each origin chronologically; process completed labels by maturity; when horizons overlap, use an explicitly delayed-feedback update. This is a validation design note for the parallel BOA implementation, not an implementation task here.
experiments.outer_gate: One same-origin, same-H paired comparison; the unchanged canonical marginal score selects. Path-dependence diagnostics have zero score weight.
experiments.cost: Weight update approximately scales with experts times matured origins; forecasting dominates when cache is absent.
risks: Immediate-feedback BOA leaks when H-step scores have not matured
Regret guarantees do not imply better absolute CRPS
Univariate quantile BOA may not match joint path scoring assumptions
Exponential forgetting can improve adaptation under drift but may remove standard asymptotic regret guarantees; only test it when drift is evidenced.
sources: Flaspohler et al. 2021 Online Learning with Optimism and Delay

experiments.contrast: Training-only TPE search of a small set of meta-parameters over frozen candidate path forecasts/loss tensors; use deterministic profiling or a small grid for one parameter.
experiments.hypothesis: Search can reduce hand-tuned meta-parameter effort without regenerating candidate forecasts for every trial.
experiments.training_protocol: Keep menu and predictions frozen; search at most pooling strength, horizon smoothness, and a justified forgetting scale using chronological inner folds; evaluate one locked setting on the next reserved block.
experiments.outer_gate: No trial selection uses reserved or full-panel outcomes; the unchanged canonical marginal score evaluates the locked result.
experiments.cost: Trials become weight/score reductions when forecast artifacts are cached; otherwise cost grows with trial count.
risks: TPE does not generate forecasts or prevent leakage
Many trials overfit repeated development requests
Pruning on noisy early-fold scores can discard good candidates
sources: Berrisch and Ziel 2024 multivariate CRPS learning

stopping_rule: Freeze recipe menu, score, origins, feature definitions, and contrasts before evaluation.

Allow one training-only tuning run per method family and one locked paired comparison on a predeclared reserved time block; record prior block reuse and do not call it independent if it has been inspected before.

Advance only candidates that improve the canonical external marginal score without forecast-integrity or within-path accounting failures; run broad checks only for survivors and a complete panel only for a survivor.
If none survives after the predeclared contrasts, close the infrastructure phase with no promotion; do not re-tune on the same 355 requests or claim universal optimality.
